figure_layouts.notes: Header inconsistency: every other column uses three header lines (rowN / thr X-Y / M/N = [...]); this figure's row2 column puts 'row2 thr 32-47' on ONE line, leaving its third header line empty. Word coordinates confirm: at top=354.4 the x=357.7 column holds 'row2 thr 32-47', at top=366.6 it holds 'M/N = [0-15]', and at top=378.8 that column is empty while the other three columns have text there. Casing/spacing inconsistency within one figure: 'k=0-31', 'k=32-63', 'k = 64 - 95', 'K = 96 - 127' (last cell uses capital K). Each k cell is drawn as a single box spanning all four VGPR rows v0..v3.
figure_layouts.title: 16x16x128 A[16][128] B[128][16], FP4

figure_layouts.notes: Spacing/casing inconsistency within one figure: 'k=0-31', 'k=0-31', 'k =32-63' (space before '='), 'K = 32-63' (capital K). Each k cell is one box spanning v0..v3. Matches the formula printed just above this figure for 32x32x64 FP4: K_L = 64 / (64 / 32) = 32.
figure_layouts.title: 32x32x64 A[32][64] B[64][32], FP4

figure_layouts.notes: Six VGPRs per operand; the grid is split into two k boxes per column: the upper box spans v0..v2 and the lower box spans v3..v5. The printed k text sits vertically next to v1 / v4 respectively but the drawn box covers three VGPR rows each — recorded as the box extent, not the text baseline. Spacing inconsistency: 'k=0-15' vs 'k = 32-47' vs 'k = 48 - 63'.
figure_layouts.title: 16x16x128 A[16][128] B[128][16], FP6

figure_layouts.notes: This figure is the continuation of the FP6 group started on printed page 51; it is the first object on printed page 52 and carries no 'FP6:' caption of its own — the caption is on the previous page. Upper box spans v0..v2, lower box spans v3..v5.
figure_layouts.title: 32x32x64 A[32][64] B[64][32], FP6

conflict_with_layout_rule.detail: CONFLICT WITH THE LAYOUT FORMULA AND WITH THE OTHER GRIDS FOR THE SAME INSTRUCTION. The cells are transcribed exactly as drawn and are NOT corrected here. dense.in.a gives K_L = 32 for both F8F6F4 shapes, so lane group g = k / 32 and item = k % 32; the eight k-boxes should read (top row) 0-31 -> 32-63 -> 64-95 -> 96-127 split half-and-half between the two VGPR halves, i.e. column g upper = 32g..32g+15 and column g lower = 32g+16..32g+31. The FP8 grids instead number the eight boxes 0-15, 16-31, 32-47, 48-63 across the UPPER row and 64-79 ... 112-127 across the LOWER row -- row-major instead of column-major. Three independent witnesses say the grid is wrong, not the formula: (1) fig.fp4.* and fig.fp6.* describe THE SAME TWO OPCODES (V_MFMA_F32_16X16X128_F8F6F4 / V_MFMA_F32_32X32X64_F8F6F4, the format being chosen at runtime by CBSZ/BLGP) and are column-major, agreeing with the formula; at most one of FP6 and FP8 can be right about which k values a lane holds. (2) fig.bf16.* and the two merge-added fig.iu8.* grids also agree with the formula, 48/48 cells. (3) the formula box printed immediately above these very figures on PDF 59 states 'A[I, k] goes in “item” k % 32 of lane I + 32 * (k / 32)'. Consumers should use dense.in.a, not these two grids.

figure_layouts.notes: Eight VGPRs; upper k box spans v0..v3, lower k box spans v4..v7.
figure_layouts.title: 16x16x128 A[16][128] B[128][16], FP8

figure_layouts.notes: Section-scope inconsistency: this is a 16-bit (BF16) layout, yet it is printed inside §7.1.5.1 'Dense Matrix Layouts: 8-bit and Smaller'. The banner row 'A[m][k]/B[k][n] Layout BF16' spans the whole table and its remaining three columns are blank. Unlike the FP4/FP6/FP8 figures, every (VGPR, column) intersection here has its own cell (no boxes spanning several VGPR rows). Column x-positions differ from the FP8/FP6 figures above (188.8 / 278.2 / 357.7 / 457.0 instead of 159.0 / 258.3 / 357.7 / 457.0) but the four columns remain row0..row3 left to right.
figure_layouts.title: A[m][k]/B[k][n] Layout BF16 — 16x16x32 A[16][32] B[32][16]

figure_layouts.notes: JOINED BY THE MERGE AGENT. Rows v0/v1 are on PDF 60 (agent C); the table restarts at the top of PDF 61 with its header repeated and rows v2/v3. PDF 61 was in agent D's range and D did not take it, so the continuation would otherwise have been lost. INCOMPLETE / TRUNCATED: this table is split across the page break. Printed page 52 (PDF 60) shows only rows v0 and v1; the table restarts on printed page 53 (PDF 61) with the same header repeated and rows v2 and v3. Rows v2/v3 are on agent D's pages and are deliberately NOT transcribed here — the merge agent must join this record with the page-53 continuation before treating it as complete. vgprs list therefore holds only the VGPRs physically on my page.
